topics.name: Conjunctions (and, but, or, so, because, since)

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct conjunction?
options: Navdeep was tired or he kept practising.
Navdeep was tired so he kept practising.
Navdeep was tired but he kept practising.
questions.rule: Being tired and still practising are opposite ideas, so join them with but.
With I, always use am: I am determined.

options: Navdeeps coach was proud of him.
Navdeep's coach was proud of him.
Navdeep coach's was proud of him.
questions.rule: To show something belongs to a person, add 's to the name: Navdeep's coach.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both always pairs with and: both javelin and shot put.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Navdeep is one person, so the present-tense verb takes -s: practises.
Waking up late is the reason, so use because.
An adverb tells how he threw: powerfully (adjective + -ly).
Subject + verb + rest: We believe in ourselves.

chat: Do you want juice or milk?
questions.rule: With I, the simple present has no -s: I want.
Ownership needs 's: Navdeep's shoes.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct conjunction?
options: We can either walk and take the bus.
We can either walk but take the bus.
We can either walk or take the bus.
questions.rule: Either always pairs with or: either walk or take the bus.
Friends is plural, so the verb has no -s: believe.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Thirst is the reason and drinking is the result. A result is joined with so.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The name belongs to my sister, so write sister's.
Every day shows a habit. With he (Navdeep), add -s: trains.
How did he speak? Use the adverb proudly.
Two opposite actions of the same person are joined with but.
Owner + 's + describing word + thing: my brother's new bat.

options: I am late because the bus broke down.
I am late so the bus broke down.
I am late or the bus broke down.
questions.rule: The bus breaking down is the reason, so use because.

chat: Does your brother play any sport?
options: Yes, he plays football every Sunday.
Yes, he play football every Sunday.
Yes, he is play football every Sunday.
questions.rule: A habit with he: verb + -s: he plays.

options: Since it was raining, so we stayed indoors.
Since it was raining, we stayed indoors.
Since it was raining, but we stayed indoors.
questions.rule: One conjunction joins two parts. Since is enough, so don't add so or but.

options: Navdeep trained very hardly for the Paralympics.
Navdeep trained very harder for the Paralympics.
Navdeep trained very hard for the Paralympics.
questions.rule: The adverb of hard is also hard. Hardly means 'almost not'.

options: The children's handprints are on the wall.
The childrens' handprints are on the wall.
The children handprints's are on the wall.
questions.rule: Children is a plural without -s, so add 's: children's.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The exam is the reason she studies, so use because.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: How did he walk? An action needs an adverb: confidently.
Wanting to go out and it being too late are opposite ideas, so use but.
Every + singular noun takes a singular verb: every athlete has.
The adverb patiently tells how he practised.

options: It is Priya handprint. She wants to help her neighbours.
It is Priya's handprint. She want to help her neighbours.
It is Priya's handprint. She wants to help her neighbours.
questions.rule: Ownership: Priya's. With she, the verb takes -s: wants.

chat: Shall we go to the park or the library?
options: Let's go to the library because it is raining.
Let's go to the library because it raining.
Let's go to the library so it is raining.
questions.rule: Rain is the reason, so use because, and keep the full verb: it is raining.

options: Navdeep received a award from the President.
Navdeep received an award from the President.
Navdeep receiving an award from the President.
questions.rule: Award begins with a vowel sound, so use an; the sentence needs a full verb: received.

options: This year's throw was more longer than last year's.
This year's throw was longest than last year's.
This year's throw was longer than last year's.
questions.rule: Comparing two things: longer than. Never more longer.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Five years is a length of time, so use for.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: When he was a boy is the past, so use the past: dreamed.
Of all compares many things, so use the most colourful.
Losing and then winning are opposite ideas, so use but.
His (possessive word) + family as subject + past verb supported + time: during tough times.
Here or means 'if not': take an umbrella, or you will get wet.

chat: What did Navdeep win in Paris?
options: He winned a gold medal in the javelin throw.
He won a gold medal in the javelin throw.
He won an gold medal in the javelin throw.
questions.rule: Win is irregular: past is won. Gold starts with a consonant sound: a gold medal.

chat: Is your brother taller than you?
options: Yes, he is taller than me, but I am faster.
Yes, he is more tall than me, but I am faster.
Yes, he is taller than me, but I am more fast.
questions.rule: Short adjectives add -er: taller, faster. Don't use more with them.

options: She didn't speak to anyone because nobody speak to her.
She didn't speak to anyone so because nobody spoke to her.
She didn't speak to anyone because nobody spoke to her.
questions.rule: One conjunction (because), and both parts in the past: didn't speak, spoke.

options: Navdeep's parents and his coach believes that he can win.
Navdeeps' parents and his coach believe that he can win.
Navdeep's parents and his coach believe that he can win.
questions.rule: Two subjects joined by and take a plural verb (believe); one owner: Navdeep's.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With he in the simple present, the verb takes -s: he wants.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: How did he listen? Use the adverb carefully.

questions.after: he did not let their words stop him.
questions.rule: He did not give up in spite of the laughter: opposite ideas take but.

questions.after: section of the library has many picture books.
questions.rule: Children is already plural, so just add 's: children's.
Navdeep's story (singular) takes gives; give something to someone.
Cause first (He worked hard), then so + result (his dreams came true).

chat: How do you feel about the award?
options: I feel proud, and I thanks everyone who believed in me.
I feels proud, and I thank everyone who believed in me.
I feel proud, and I thank everyone who believed in me.
questions.rule: With I, the simple present has no -s: I feel, I thank.

chat: Can you come to the stadium today?
options: I can't come today because I have a test tomorrow.
I can't come today because I has a test tomorrow.
I can't came today because I have a test tomorrow.
questions.rule: After can't, use the base verb (come); with I, use have.
